Hero (title + slogan + Get started button + real syntax-highlighted SELECT SQL example); version switcher (v2.4 / v2.3 / v2.2 / v2.1); ⌘K search; three quick-start cards (Install / Connect / Your first query); 6 docs-section cards (Architecture / SQL Syntax / Functions / Data Types / Storage / Extensions); dark / light theme toggle. - `reference.html` — Reference main entry. **Three-column layout**: left deep TOC tree (Schemas / Tables / Views / Indexes / Functions [Aggregate / String / Numeric / Date-Time / JSON / Window sub-groups] / Operators [category sub-groups], nodes expandable / collapsible); center reference overview + popular links + v2.4 new-features callout; right-side on-this-page outline. - `function-date-trunc.html` — DATE_TRUNC function detail page (**canonical example spec**). Three-column layout; signature code block; parameter table; return value; 3 SQL examples with result tables (basic usage / GROUP BY pairing / nested EXTRACT); error-case callouts; collapsible version-history panel (added v1.0, microsecond un

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore Tessera’s documentation/tutorial UX, with emphasis on the primary onboarding path from home to SQL/reference content, while validating adjacent navigation, version switching, search/theme controls, and mobile usability risks.
run_plan.summary: Start on the docs home page and verify the main onboarding path: hero CTA, quick-start cards, and the key documentation categories that branch into SQL syntax, reference, data types, and function detail pages. Then spend most of the run in the reference and function pages, checking category navigation, deep links, example blocks, and collapsible/versioned content for consistency and recoverability. Finally, repeat the most important interactions in a mobile viewport to confirm the known small tap targets and unlabeled select/search controls do not break navigation.
assumptions: The known HTML files in the prescan represent the full in-scope site coverage for this run.

Top navigation items like Tutorials, Download, and GitHub appear to be placeholder links on the docs home and should be treated as possible dead-end or no-op controls unless they resolve during execution.
The search and version switcher are visible site-wide, but the prescan does not prove a real search results page exists; validate interaction behavior rather than assuming search-driven navigation.

The reference sidebar is expected to expand/collapse in-place and may reveal many linked pages not listed as separate HTML files; if those links route to known files, prioritize coverage of the listed pages.
Mobile validation should focus on responsiveness and tap-target accessibility rather than a full alternate information architecture.
risk_hotspots: index.html: version selector (unlabeled select), ⌘K search button, theme toggle, and small top-nav tap targets on mobile
index.html: placeholder/hash links for Tutorials, Download, GitHub, and some quick-start/documentation cards
reference.html: expandable left TOC tree for Schemas/Tables/Views/Indexes/Functions/Operators, especially if nested items collapse or become hard to hit
function-date-trunc.html: canonical example page with signature, examples, error callouts, and version-history panel; high risk for dense content and collapsible state
function-json-extract.html: JSON path examples and any advanced JSON behavior implied by v2.4 notes
function-regexp-match.html: RE2 syntax details, flags, and edge-case examples
function-row-number.html: window-function semantics and version history panel
operators.html: category tables and precedence ordering, especially if long content creates navigation or readability issues
sql-select.html: syntax ordering, clause explanations, and examples with copy/code blocks

key_checks: Repeat the home-page version selector, search, theme toggle, and primary CTAs on mobile
Verify the reference TOC can be expanded and used without accidental taps or clipping
Check that dense tables, code blocks, and example sections remain legible and scrollable

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 9 known HTML pages, with deeper interaction on the 5 content-heavy docs pages plus home and reference entry.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise the visible global controls, at least one navigation interaction per major page, and most visible section/expand/collapse controls on reference and function pages.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the critical onboarding, reference browsing, and dense-content reading checks in a mobile viewport, prioritizing the small-tap-target and unlabeled-select risks.

notes: Because the prescan shows no console or network errors, the run should prioritize interaction quality, navigation depth, and accessibility rather than failure recovery.
Treat the site as a docs system first: success means users can learn, browse, and compare pages without getting stuck, not just that links open.

observation.title: SELECT statement — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array SELECT statement SELECT is the workhorse of Tessera. Its clauses are evaluated in a fixed order even though they may be written in any order in the source text. Syntax SELECT [DISTINCT] expression FROM source [WHERE] predicate [GROUP BY] expression [HAVING] predicate [ORDER BY] expression [LIMIT] n [OFFSET] n WITH Common table expressions for readability and recursion. Copy WITH recent AS ( SELECT id, amount_cents FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-01' ) SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM recent; FROM Sources can be tables, subqueries, table-valued functions, or external file readers. Copy SELECT * FROM read_parquet('s3://bucket/orders/*.parquet'); WHERE Row-level filter applied before grouping. Supports any expression returning BOOLEAN. GROUP BY Groups rows by the listed expressions. SELECT items must be aggregates or referenced in GROUP BY. HAVING Post-grouping filter, evaluated after aggregates compute. ORDER BY Sorts the final result. Supports ASC / DESC and NULLS FIRST / LAST. LIMIT and OFFSET Restricts the row count. OFFSET can be expensive on large result sets — prefer cursor pagination. Performance tip. Push column projection and filters into your storage layer when reading from Parquet — Tessera's read_parquet applies predicate pushdown automatically when supported. Examples Copy -- Top spenders this quarter SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount_cents) AS total FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-04-01' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount_cents) > 100000 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 20; ON THIS PAGE Syntax WITH FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER BY LIMIT Examples © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

Copy SELECT * FROM read_parquet('s3://bucket/orders/*.parquet'); WHERE Row-level filter applied before grouping. Supports any expression returning BOOLEAN. GROUP BY Groups rows by the listed expressions. SELECT items must be aggregates or referenced in GROUP BY. HAVING Post-grouping filter, evaluated after aggregates compute. ORDER BY Sorts the final result. Supports ASC / DESC and NULLS FIRST / LAST. LIMIT and OFFSET Restricts the row count. OFFSET can be expensive on large result sets — prefer cursor pagination. Performance tip. Push column projection and filters into your storage layer when reading from Parquet — Tessera's read_parquet applies predicate pushdown automatically when supported. Examples Copy -- Top spenders this quarter SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount_cents) AS total FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-04-01' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount_cents) > 100000 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 20; ON THIS PAGE Syntax WITH FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER BY LIMIT Examples © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. observation.title: DATE_TRUNC — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. Related functions EXTRACT DATE_ADD NOW CAST CURRENT_DATE AGE ON THIS PAGE Signature Parameters Return value Examples Errors Version history Related © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. REGEXP_MATCH evaluates to TRUE when pattern matches anywhere in the input string. Anchor with ^ and $ for full-string matches. Signature REGEXP_MATCH(string TEXT, pattern TEXT [, flags TEXT]) → BOOLEAN Parameters Name Type Required Description string TEXT required The string to test. pattern TEXT required A RE2-compatible regular expression. flags TEXT optional Optional flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 's' dotall, 'm' multiline. Return value TRUE if the pattern matches anywhere in the string, FALSE otherwise. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL. Examples 1. Simple match Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('service-12', '^service-\d+$'); Result regexp_match true 2. Case insensitive match with flag Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('ABC123', '^abc', 'i'); Result regexp_match true 3. observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub ROW_NUMBER Assign a unique sequential integer to each row within a window partition. ROW_NUMBER is the simplest of the ranking window functions. Unlike RANK, ties do not share a number. Signature ROW_NUMBER() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...) → BIGINT Parameters Name Type Required Description OVER clause WINDOW required Defines the window. Top-N per partition A common pattern: find the latest event per user. observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub ROW_NUMBER Assign a unique sequential integer to each row within a window partition. ROW_NUMBER is the simplest of the ranking window functions. Unlike RANK, ties do not share a number. Signature ROW_NUMBER() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...) → BIGINT Parameters Name Type Required Description OVER clause WINDOW required Defines the window. PARTITION BY is optional; ORDER BY is required. Return value BIGINT starting at 1 for each new partition. Examples 1. Number all rows by created_at Copy SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY created_at) AS rn FROM orders; Result id rn ord_001 1 ord_002 2 ord_003 3 2. Top-N per partition A common pattern: find the latest event per user. Copy WITH ranked AS ( SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY created_at DESC) AS rn FROM events ) SELECT user_id, type, created_at FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1; Result user_id type created_at u_001 login 2026-05-11 14:22:08 u_002 purchase 2026-05-11 12:45:01 3. Distinguishes ties (vs RANK) Copy SELECT score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS rn, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS rk FROM leaderboard; Result score rn rk 95 1 1 95 2 1 90 3 3 Version history 2 entries ▼ v2.3Parallel evaluation of partitioned ROW_NUMBER across cores. v1.0Added in v1.0. observation.title: Tessera — The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics.
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 v2.4 · 2026-04 release The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics. Tessera runs in your process, reads Parquet and CSV directly, and ships SIMD-optimized vector kernels for sub-millisecond aggregation over millions of rows. Get started → View reference SELECT SELECT region, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM read_parquet('orders/*.parquet') WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC; Quick start 1 Install Drop-in single-file build for Linux, macOS, Windows. No service to run. 2 Connect Open a file-backed or in-memory database with one line in your language of choice. 3 Your first query Run analytical queries directly on Parquet, CSV, and Arrow data. Documentation Architecture Storage, vectorized execution, and query planning. SQL Syntax Statements, expressions, and railroad diagrams. Functions Scalar, aggregate, window, and string functions. Data Types Native and extended types with storage details. Storage Page format, WAL, snapshots, and replication. Extensions Geospatial, JSON, vector search, and full-text. © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.title: DATE_TRUNC — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. Related functions EXTRACT DATE_ADD NOW CAST CURRENT_DATE AGE ON THIS PAGE Signature Parameters Return value Examples Errors Version history Related © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.title: JSON_EXTRACT — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub JSON_EXTRACT Extract a value from a JSON document using a JSONPath expression. JSON_EXTRACT navigates a JSON document with JSONPath. The result is a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null). Signature JSON_EXTRACT(document JSON, path TEXT) → JSON Parameters Name Type Required Description document JSON required A JSON document. Strings will be auto-parsed if they contain valid JSON. path TEXT required A JSONPath expression beginning with $. Return value A JSON scalar or composite value. Use ::TEXT or ::INTEGER to cast to a SQL type. Examples 1. Extract a string field Copy SELECT JSON_EXTRACT('{"user":{"name":"Ana","plan":"pro"}}'::JSON, '$.user.name'); Result json_extract "Ana" 2. Extract from JSON column in table Copy SELECT id, JSON_EXTRACT(payload, '$.event.type')::TEXT AS event_type, JSON_EXTRACT(payload, '$.event.amount')::INTEGER AS amount FROM events WHERE JSON_EXTRACT(payload, '$.event.type') = '"charge.succeeded"'; Result id event_type amount ev_8Hk2nF charge.succeeded 2500 ev_M5kQ2nF charge.succeeded 1899 3. Array indexing Copy SELECT JSON_EXTRACT('{"items":[10,20,30]}'::JSON, '$.items[1]'); Result json_extract 20 Errors Common errors: invalid_path: malformed JSONPath expression. type_mismatch: attempting to cast a non-scalar JSON value to a primitive SQL type. Version history 3 entries ▼ v2.4JSONPath now supports filter expressions like $.items[?(@.price > 100)]. v2.2Improved index access performance for large arrays by ~3×. v1.5Added in v1.5. Related functions JSON_VALID JSON_AGG JSON_OBJECT JSON_ARRAY JSON_TYPE CAST ON THIS PAGE Signature Parameters Return value Examples Errors Version history Related © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.title: DATE_TRUNC — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. Related functions EXTRACT DATE_ADD NOW CAST CURRENT_DATE AGE ON THIS PAGE Signature Parameters Return value Examples Errors Version history Related © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub REGEXP_MATCH Test whether a string matches a regular expression using the RE2 syntax. REGEXP_MATCH evaluates to TRUE when pattern matches anywhere in the input string. Anchor with ^ and $ for full-string matches. Signature REGEXP_MATCH(string TEXT, pattern TEXT [, flags TEXT]) → BOOLEAN Parameters Name Type Required Description string TEXT required The string to test. pattern TEXT required A RE2-compatible regular expression. flags TEXT optional Optional flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 's' dotall, 'm' multiline. Return value TRUE if the pattern matches anywhere in the string, FALSE otherwise. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL. Examples 1. Simple match Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('service-12', '^service-\d+$'); Result regexp_match true 2. Case insensitive match with flag Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('ABC123', '^abc', 'i'); Result regexp_match true 3. Filter rows matching pattern Copy SELECT email FROM customers WHERE REGEXP_MATCH(email, '^.+@example\.(com|org)$'); Result email ana@example.com julien@example.org nora@example.com Errors Common errors: invalid_regex: malformed pattern (unbalanced parens, invalid escape). regex_timeout: pattern took longer than 100ms to evaluate. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Pattern cache size raised from 256 to 1024 entries. v2.0Switched regex engine from PCRE to RE2 for predictable execution time. Some lookbehinds no longer supported. v1.5Added flags parameter. v1.0Added in initial release. No service to run. 2 Connect Open a file-backed or in-memory database with one line in your language of choice. 3 Your first query Run analytical queries directly on Parquet, CSV, and Arrow data. Documentation Architecture Storage, vectorized execution, and query planning. SQL Syntax Statements, expressions, and railroad diagrams. Functions Scalar, aggregate, window, and string functions. Data Types Native and extended types with storage details. Storage Page format, WAL, snapshots, and replication. Extensions Geospatial, JSON, vector search, and full-text. © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.title: Tessera — The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics.
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 v2.4 · 2026-04 release The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics. Tessera runs in your process, reads Parquet and CSV directly, and ships SIMD-optimized vector kernels for sub-millisecond aggregation over millions of rows. Get started → View reference SELECT SELECT region, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM read_parquet('orders/*.parquet') WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC; Quick start 1 Install Drop-in single-file build for Linux, macOS, Windows. No service to run. 2 Connect Open a file-backed or in-memory database with one line in your language of choice. 3 Your first query Run analytical queries directly on Parquet, CSV, and Arrow data. Documentation Architecture Storage, vectorized execution, and query planning. SQL Syntax Statements, expressions, and railroad diagrams. Functions Scalar, aggregate, window, and string functions. Data Types Native and extended types with storage details. Storage Page format, WAL, snapshots, and replication. Extensions Geospatial, JSON, vector search, and full-text. © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.title: DATE_TRUNC — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. Related functions EXTRACT DATE_ADD NOW CAST CURRENT_DATE AGE ON THIS PAGE Signature Parameters Return value Examples Errors Version history Related © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. observation.title: Tessera — The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics.
observation.visible_text: Tessera v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 v2.4 · 2026-04 release The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics. Tessera runs in your process, reads Parquet and CSV directly, and ships SIMD-optimized vector kernels for sub-millisecond aggregation over millions of rows. Get started → View reference SELECT SELECT region, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM read_parquet('orders/*.parquet') WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC; Quick start 1 Install Drop-in single-file build for Linux, macOS, Windows. No service to run. 2 Connect Open a file-backed or in-memory database with one line in your language of choice. 3 Your first query Run analytical queries directly on Parquet, CSV, and Arrow data. Documentation Architecture Storage, vectorized execution, and query planning. SQL Syntax Statements, expressions, and railroad diagrams. Functions Scalar, aggregate, window, and string functions. Data Types Native and extended types with storage details. Storage Page format, WAL, snapshots, and replication. Extensions Geospatial, JSON, vector search, and full-text. © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.
